instructions: Heat a Dutch oven or heavy soup pot over medium-high heat with 1 tsp of the oil. Slice the mushrooms, add them with 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, until they're browned and the liquid has cooked off, about 8 minutes. Transfer them to a bowl.
Cut the beef into 1/2-inch pieces and pat them dry. Season with 3/4 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.

Heat another 1 tsp of the oil in the pot until it shimmers. Brown the beef for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then. It doesn't need to be cooked through. Transfer it to the bowl with the mushrooms.
Add the remaining 1 tsp oil to the pot, then the diced celery, onion, parsnips and carrots and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, until they're slightly softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, oregano, basil and bay leaf and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Return the beef and mushrooms to the pot with the tomatoes and their juice and the broth. Bring it to a boil.
Stir in the barley, turn the heat down to a simmer, cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Strip the kale from its stems and chop about 3 cups of the leaves. Stir the kale into the soup and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Take out the bay leaf. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt and the remaining 1/4 tsp pepper.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 4 days, and the soup freezes for up to 3 months. The barley keeps soaking up broth, so add a splash of broth or water when you reheat it.
method_notes: Lead is Garlic and Zest (4.2 from 21): mushrooms and beef browned separately, then the vegetables, tomatoes and broth, with pearl barley added and kale at the end. Scaled from 8 servings down to 4. Pearl barley is used, not quick-cooking, so the beef has time to get tender. The browning sauce is left out. It's a batch soup, over an hour from start to finish.
